msg.content:
<document>
<title>Avatar: The Way of Water</title>
<fragment>

Outside the US and Canada, the film grossed $307.6 million in 52 countries in its first week of release. The largest openings for the film by the end of the week were in China ($56.8 million), South Korea ($24.9 million), France ($21.7 million), Germany ($19.4 million) and India ($19.2 million).[211][212] In the second weekend, it grossed $168.6 million for a drop of 42%.[241] In the third weekend, it grossed $186.7 million, an increase of 6% from the previous weekend.[242] In the fourth weekend, it grossed $132.6 million for a drop of 30%, while becoming the highest-grossing film of the pandemic era outside the US and Canada.[243] The five largest-running total countries by February 26, 2023, are China ($249.8 million), France ($148.3 million), Germany ($138.3 million), South Korea ($105 million) and the United Kingdom ($91 million). It became the highest-grossing film of all time in twenty box office territories, including Germany, France, Austria, Turkey and New Zealand.[244][245][246][247]




</fragment>
<fragment>

It is the fourth film to reach the $1 billion milestone in the pandemic era after *Spider-Man: No Way Home*, *Top Gun: Maverick* and *Jurassic World Dominion*, as well as the sixth-fastest overall to reach the milestone at 14 days.[216][217] It crossed the $2 billion milestone on January 22, becoming the first film in the pandemic era and the sixth in history to reach the milestone. It is also the second-fastest to gross over $2 billion, reaching the milestone in 40 days.[218][219] *Deadline Hollywood* calculated the film's net profit as $531.7 million, accounting for production budgets, marketing, talent participations and other costs; box office grosses and home media revenues placed it first on their list of 2022's "Most Valuable Blockbusters".[220]



#### United States and Canada[edit]


</fragment>
<fragment>

![](image)Theater attendees watching the film in 3D in Barcelona
*Avatar: The Way of Water* grossed $684.1 million in the United States and Canada, and $1.636 billion in other territories, for a worldwide total of $2.320 billion.[4][5] It had a worldwide opening of $441.7 million, the eleventh-biggest of all time, and the third largest in the COVID-19 pandemic era, behind *Spider-Man: No Way Home* ($601 million) and *Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness* ($452.4 million). IMAX accounted for $48.8 million, the second-highest global weekend ever for a film released in IMAX cinemas.[211][212] It is the highest-grossing film of 2022, the third-highest-grossing film of all time,[213][214] and the highest-grossing film of the pandemic era.[215]


</fragment>
<fragment>
214. **^** "All Time Worldwide Box Office". *The Numbers*. Archived from the original on February 19, 2023. Retrieved January 8, 2023.
215. **^** Kay, Jeremy (January 17, 2023). "'Avatar: The Way Of Water' confirmed as highest global pandemic era hit, sixth highest of all time". *Screen International*. Archived from the original on January 17, 2023. Retrieved January 18, 2023.
216. **^** McClintock, Pamela (December 28, 2022). "Box Office Milestone: 'Avatar 2' Crosses $1B Globally in 14 Days". *The Hollywood Reporter*. Archived from the original on December 28, 2022. Retrieved December 28, 2022.
217. **^** "Avatar The Way of Water box office: James Cameron movie crosses $1 billion in 14 days; 6th fastest film ever to do so". *Hindustan Times*. December 28, 2022. Archived from the original on December 29, 2022. Retrieved December 29, 2022.

</fragment>
</document>

Including revenue from the 2012, 2017 and 2023 reissues, *Titanic* earned $674.3 million in North America and $1.583 billion in other countries, for a worldwide total of $2.257 billion.[Note 1][14] It became the highest-grossing film of all time worldwide in 1998, beating *Jurassic Park* (1993).[105] The film remained so for twelve years, until *Avatar* (2009), also written and directed by Cameron, surpassed it in 2010.[106] On March 1, 1998,[107] it became the first film to earn more than $1 billion worldwide[108] and on the weekend April 13–15, 2012—a century after the original vessel's foundering, *Titanic* became the second film to cross the $2 billion threshold during its 3D re-release.[109] Box Office Mojo estimates that *Titanic* is the fifth-highest-grossing film of all time in North America when adjusting for ticket price inflation.[110] The site also estimates that the film sold over 128 million tickets in the US in its initial theatrical run.[111]


</fragment>
<fragment>
The Numbers does not log individual releases, but had the lifetime total recorded as $2.186 billion in September 2014 (roughly equating to $1.843 billion for the original release and $343.6 million for the 3D reissue).[11] A couple of weeks later, The Numbers increased the lifetime gross to $2.208 billion, without explanation.[12] Prior to the 2023 re-release, the totals at both trackers were inflated above the true figure. For clarity, *Titanic* earned $1.843 billion on its original release, $344 million from its 2012 reissue, $691,642 from the 2017 reissue, and $71,352 in 2020, for a lifetime total of $2,187,687,082 from the first four releases. Along with the $70.2 million grossed from the 25th anniversary re-release in 2023,[13] the lifetime total for *Titanic* stands at $2,257,844,554 as of May 22, 2023[update].
2. **^** Although the *Titanic* hit the iceberg on April 14, it did not sink until the early hours of April 15.

Its highest grossing single day was Saturday, February 14, 1998, on which it earned $13,048,711, more than eight weeks after its North American debut.[117][118] On March 14, it surpassed *Star Wars* as the highest-grossing film ever in North America.[119] It stayed at number one for 15 consecutive weeks in North America, a record for any film.[120] By April 1998, the film's number one spot would be overtaken by *Lost in Space*, dropping into second place.[121] The film stayed in theaters in North America for almost 10 months before finally closing on Thursday, October 1, 1998, with a final domestic gross of $600,788,188,[122] equivalent to $1140.3  million in 2023[123]. Outside North America, the film made double its North American gross, generating $1,242,413,080[124] and accumulating a grand total of $1,843,201,268 worldwide from its initial theatrical run.[125]

content:
**Production budgets (USD millions)**  

| Rank (by worldwide gross) | Film (release year) | Reported production budget* |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | *Avatar* (2009) | **$237 M** |
| 2 | *Avatar: The Way of Water* (2022) | **$350 M** (est. $350–$460 M) |
| 3 | *Titanic* (1997) | **$200 M** |
| 4 | *Star Wars: The Force Awakens* (2015) | **$245 M** |
| 5 | *Avengers: Endgame* (2019) | **$356 M** |

\*Budgets are taken from the *Wikipedia* articles for each film (the “Budget” entry in the infobox). Wikipedia reports the figures as follows:

* **Avatar** – $237 million (see *Avatar* page).  
* **Avatar: The Way of Water** – $350 million (the infobox lists a range of $350–$460 million; the lower‑bound figure is commonly quoted).  
* **Titanic** – $200 million (the *Titanic (1997 film)* page lists a $200 M production budget).  
* **Star Wars: The Force Awakens** – $245 million (the *Star Wars: The Force Awakens* page).  
* **Avengers: Endgame** – $356 million (the *Avengers: Endgame* page).

These numbers represent the production (principal‑photography) costs only; they do **not** include marketing, distribution, or ancillary expenses. All amounts are expressed in 2025 U.S. dollars (i.e., the nominal values reported in the sources).
